findings.summary: The applicant Department select shows an error description without exposing its invalid state programmatically.
findings.fix: When a department error exists, add aria-invalid="true" to the select along with its existing aria-describedby reference; omit both error attributes when valid.
findings.evidence: The select conditionally references teacher-lifecycle-department_id-error but never sets aria-invalid.

findings.summary: The performance-review Teacher error is not associated with its select, so assistive technology may not announce the error with the field.
findings.fix: Give the error paragraph an ID and conditionally reference it with aria-describedby on the select; also set aria-invalid="true" while the error exists.
findings.evidence: The Teacher error paragraph has no ID, and the select has neither aria-describedby nor aria-invalid.

findings.summary: The performance-review rating select references its error text but does not expose its invalid state.
findings.fix: Conditionally add aria-invalid="true" when the rating error exists, alongside the existing error description reference.
findings.evidence: The rating select references teacher-lifecycle-rating-error but never sets aria-invalid.

findings.summary: A resignation Teacher validation error is generated server-side but is not rendered beside or associated with the select.
findings.fix: Render the teacher_id error as visible text with a unique ID, reference it from the select with aria-describedby, and set aria-invalid="true" while the error exists.
findings.evidence: The server sets fieldErrors['teacher_id'] for schedule_resignation, but this select has no error rendering or error-state attributes.

findings.summary: When a form reopens after field-level validation errors without a global error summary, focus goes to the first field rather than the first invalid field.
findings.fix: On error-driven modal reopening, focus a rendered error summary or the first [aria-invalid="true"] control; ensure every field error is visible and programmatically associated.
findings.evidence: The modal selects the first input, select, or textarea; fieldErrors do not create data-error-summary, and the later focus fallback does not target lifecycle-form errors.

passed: Applicant, performance-review, and resignation controls have visible, programmatically associated labels.
Required controls use native required attributes and visible Required indicators.
All three form panels are configured to reopen their modal after server-side validation errors.
